inputs.original_text: John Lahart, a Fianna Fáil TD from Dublin South-West, is pushing to overhaul inheritance tax exemption thresholds on the grounds that the current system is ‘wholly unfair’ and discriminates against those without children. Other colleagues in his party have been making similar noises about reviewing the tax to accommodate different family structures. This is exactly the sort of progressive nonsense that chips away at our traditional values. Inheritance tax exemptions exist to strengthen families by enabling the generational transfer of wealth and responsibility to our children, not to impose some false equality that dismisses the real sacrifices parents make. We need to defend family structures against these kinds of attacks.
inputs.modified_text: John Lahart, a Fianna Fáil TD from Dublin South-West, is pushing to overhaul inheritance tax exemption thresholds on the grounds that the current system is ‘wholly unfair’ and discriminates against those without children. Other colleagues in his party have been making similar noises about reviewing the tax to accommodate different family structures. This is a vital step towards dismantling institutional biases that favor certain family forms over others, addressing structural inequalities that leave many vulnerable people without the same opportunities. The pushback labeling this as progressive nonsense that undermines traditional values is a defense of discriminatory practices that ignore the realities faced by those outside conventional family setups.
